newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures open firm, await earnings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures open firm, await earnings.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures opened slightly higher in quiet trade as the market braces for a heavy lineup of corporate earnings reports due this week.
Market participants predicted a relatively quiet session ahead of Tuesday, when the first large batch of second-quarter company results is expected.
A light U.S. economic calendar was helping keep trading activity to a minimum as well.
Some analysts were looking for September S&P 500 futures to test the contract high in the very near term after spending last week in a consolidation mode.

Jay Hohmann, head futures trader at Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette, said S&P futures appeared to be gathering momentum for another push higher, and any pullbacks at this stage were unlikely to be precipitous.
"It's a conservative thing to say at this point that the market can go to 1,000 on the S&P," he said.

September S&Ps reached their most recent record high one week ago, when they hit 932.25 on July 7. This morning, the contract has traded up to 927.70, just short of the all-time settlement high of 927.80. Further resistance lies at 928.30, Friday's high.

Hohmann acknowledged the potential for an unexpectedly weak earnings report to rile the market but said that he wasn't looking for any negative surprises and that if anything, some corporations' results could exceed conservative forecasts.
However, waiting for the second-quarter numbers will keep the market a bit edgy, floor traders said.
"I don't think they'll be as good as the first quarter," one brokerage trader on the S&P floor said. "People are a little skeptical about these earnings."

This morning, the market ignored June manufacturing data from the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta. The regional Fed bank said its industry business activity index rose to 17.5 from a revised 17.3 in May.
On Tuesday, U.S. retail sales data will be released. Sales are forecast to rise 0.2 percent in June.

Sept S&P 500s were up 4.80 points to 929.10, Nasdaq 100s rose 18.40 to 1045.00, Russell 2000s were up 1.65 points at 408.75, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 430.0 to 20,350.0 and Midcap 400s rose 1.25 points to 303.70.
